html:
The Grand Principality of Moscow, or Muscovy, was the Russian state that grew from a small town into the core of Russia, between the late 1200s and 1547. The map shows it in 1300, 1492 and 1500.

Moscow became a separate principality under Daniel, a son of Alexander Nevsky. Its princes rose by serving the Golden Horde: Ivan I collected tribute for the khans, and the head of the Russian church moved to Moscow in 1325. In 1380 Dmitry Donskoy beat a Tatar army at the Battle of Kulikovo.

Ivan III made it a large state. He annexed Novgorod in 1478, stopped paying the Horde, and faced it down at the Great Stand on the Ugra River in 1480. He married a niece of the last Byzantine emperor and brought Italian architects to rebuild the Kremlin. In 1547 his grandson Ivan IV was crowned tsar, and the state became the Tsardom of Russia.
